Banerjee, B.Sc., B.H.M.S. (B.U.) and on its perusal it transpires that this doctor is a Homeopathy doctor and the 
management has filed these prescriptions with a view to prove the contradiction in the statement of the applicant 
Bijay Bauri because he had stated that he was providing treatment to his wife by an Ayurvedic doctor in his village 
whereas the prescription was found of a Homeopathy doctor. 


The Management has also submitted a photo copy of commendation/punishment and on its perusal it 
transpires that this is details of commendation/punishment (if any) and it shows that there is deduction of two annual 
increments and in punishment column/ details of the offence:-“long absent has been mentioned” and thereafter “basic 
before punishment = 1377.20 and basic after deduction of two increments = 1298.15” has been mentioned. It further 
transpires that it has been attested by someone putting his signature as well as date but without any Designation and 
stamp and it appears that the management has filed this document to prove that the workman Bijay Bauri was a 
habitual absentee but this document cannot be relied for the reason that neither this document bears the name of Bijay 
Bauri nor the period of absence nor date and duration of the absence, has been mentioned and therefore being only 
photo copy of some descriptions it cannot be read against the workman Bijay Bauri for the reasons stated above. 


Now as regards the documentary evidence adduced from the side of the workman, Exhibit W-1 is the copy of 
charge sheet dated 02.04.2019 issued by the Disciplinary Authority cum Management Amalgamated Dhansar 
Industry Colliery to the workman Sri Bijay Bauri mentioning therein that written report was received against him that 
he remained absent without taking leave or permission from duty from 21.02.2018 which was misconduct as per CSO 
of the company under clause 26.1.1 and he has been directed to file explanation within 15 days from the date of 
receipt of this charge sheet. Exhibit W-2 is the dismissal order dated 11/13.09.2019 that has been issued by the Project 
Officer Dhansar Industry Colliery to the applicant Bijay Bauri in which it has been described that due to remaining 
unauthorizedly absent from duty since 21.02.2018 a charge sheet was issued under CSO No. 26.1.1 on 02.04.2019 
against Bijay Bauri and he also submitted explanation for the same but it was not found satisfactory and therefore 
enquiry proceeding was conducted in which he also participated and after the conclusion it was found that the charges 
levelled against him was true. Thereafter he was again issued second show cause notice on 08.05.2019 but his 
explanation for the same was also not found satisfactory and ultimately considering all these points holding him guilty 
of being absent without any information from duty he was dismissed from the service of the company with immediate 
effect and he was further informed that within 30 days from the date of receipt of dismissal order he can file appeal to 
the notified authority. Exhibit W-3 are the copies of prescriptions of the patient Mina Bauri wife of Bijay Bauri dated 
17.02.2018, 19.05.18, 30.06.18, 20.10.18, 29.11.18, 29.03.19,24.06.19 and 16.09.19 of Dr. A. Banerjee, B.Sc., 
B.H.M.S. (B.U.) and on its perusal it transpires that this doctor is a Homeopathy doctor. Exhibit W-4 is mercy appeal 
dated 06.11.2019 that has been filed by the workman Bijay Bauri addressed to Project Officer Dhansar Colliery in 
which he has admitted that due to his wife’s sudden illness he remained busy in her treatment and could not give 
information to the management and he has admitted his fault and assured not to make this fault again and has 
requested to set aside the dismissal order and permit him to go to his work and Exhibit W-5 
is the second show cause notice dated 08.05.2019 issued by the Management/Project Officer to Bijay Bauri by which 
he has been informed that he has been found guilty in the finding of the enquiry and he has been suggested to submit 
any left evidence or defence if the same could not be submitted by him previously within 15 days of the receipt of this 
notice. 


12. Thus, on the basis of above discussions of the documentary evidence adduced from the side of the workman as 
well management this Tribunal finds that the workman Bijay Bauri remained absent from his duty since 21.02.2018 
without giving any information and taking permission from the management that he has also admitted by accepting 
the enquiry proceeding as fair and proper but as regards the quantum of punishment awarded to the workman Bijay 
Bauri by the management, that is not proportionate to the misconduct of Bijay Bauri as there is no cogent and reliable 
evidence on record that the applicant Bijay Bauri has been a habitual absentee and for want of the same, the order of 
dismissal passed by the management is held quite disproportionate and therefore it is held that the action of the 
management of Dhansar Industry Colliery under Kusunda Area of M/s. BCCL in dismissing Sri Bijay Bauri Ex. 
General Mazdoor from his service w.e.f. 13.09.2019 is neither legal nor justified rather quite disproportionate. 


13. Hence, the order of dismissal dated 11/13.09.2019 is hereby set aside and the Management of BCCL is directed 
to reinstate the workman Bijay Bauri in the services of the Company within one month from the date of notification of 
this Award. The workman shall be entitled to all other consequential benefits but he will not be entitled to any 
increment or back wages during period of absence from duty.

Central Government vide Notification No.L-2201 1/13/2015-IR(CM-II) dated 31.08.2015, under sub-section 
(1) and sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (hereinafter called the Act), has referred 
the following Industrial dispute for adjudication to this Tribunal:- 


“Whether the action of the management of Food Corporation of India in taking the date of birth of 
workmen as shown in the seniority list of the Bajaj Committee Report is legal and justified? If not, what 
relief the workman is entitled and from which date?” 


1. Brief facts of the case as per claim statement filed on behalf of workers union are that the Food Corporation 
of India (hereinafter called as FCI) is a statutory corporation set up by the Government of India under Section 3 of 
Food Corporations Act, 1964. In order to carry out its business, FCI initially engaged the contract workers in its 
godowns/depots and then in due course of time, it departmentalized the contract workers or brought them under the 
Direct Payment System of No Work No Pay System, thereby bringing them under the direct employer/employee 
relationship with it. The job of such workers consists of loading, unloading, stacking, de-stacking, weighment, 
salvaging and standardization of food grains. The FCI also gets the aforesaid food handling operations carried out 
through the contract workers or through its own workers at railheads and railway sidings as well. Respondent 10.1 & 
2 manage and control the affairs of the FCI at regional level and district level respectively.

2 Pursuant of issuance of notification dated 29.11.1985 by Government of Haryana under Section 10 of the 
Contract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) Act, 1970, employment of contract labour in 22 depots of FCI in Haryana 
was directed to be prohibited, which notification was challenged upto Hon'ble Supreme Court and was upheld by it. 
Accordingly, a committee was established to look into the grievances and in pursuance of the report made by the 
committee contract labour system was abolished in 22 depots of FCI including FCI, Karnal complex. 


3. Subsequent to the abolition of contract labour system in 22 depots of FCI, Haryana, a bipartite settlement 
dated 12.04.1991 (Annexure W/4) was entered into between the FCI and workers union for the regularization of the 
contract workers. The question arose as to the identification and seniority of workers for the purpose of their 
departmentalization in accordance with the requisite labour strength of FCI. The FCI headquarter then came out with 
a circular no.IRL/8(1)(91) dated 11.06.1991 (Annexure W/5) prescribing the methodology/modus operandi for the 
identification and determination of seniority for the purpose of departmentalization. A detailed procedure for the 
identification of the contract workers has been laid down in paragraph no.3.1 of the aforesaid circular dated 
11.06.1991. Paragraph 4.2 of the aforesaid circular provides for the determination of seniority as per the length of 
service of a worker with the contractor. It further provides that if documentary proof of the age of a worker is not 
available, a medical check up to determine his age should be carried out or alternatively the worker may be referred to 
the local Government of Municipal hospital for determination of his age, if no documentary proof of the same is 
available. 


4. In pursuance of the aforesaid circular dated 11.06.1991, various committees namely Dalela Committee-I, 
Dalela Committee-I]], Chopra Committee and Ranga Committee were formed one by one to settle/finalize the 
seniority of the workers so as to regularize them against the regular vacancies in FCI, Karnal. It is stated that the FCI, 
Zonal Office (North) vide order dated 29.07.1991 fixed the strength of 251 workers for FCI, Karnal. Finally, Mr. R. 
K. Ranga, the then Senior Regional Manager, FCI, Regional Office, Haryana under the directions of the Hon’ble 
High Court of Punjab & Haryana determined the inter se seniority of the works of FCI, Karnal vide order dated 
28.04.1994 and departmentalized such workers against 251 regular vacancies. 


By The order/report dated 28.04.1994 of Mr. R. K. Ranga was challenged in a CWP bearing No.11647 of 1994 
titled as Ram Rattan and others Versus Food Corporation of India and others filed before the Hon’ble High Court 
of Punjab & Haryana. The Hon’ble High Court of Punjab & Haryana vide order dated 08.01.2009 (Annexure W/6) 
quashed the order dated 28.04.1994 of Mr. Ranga and appointed Sh. R. P. Bajaj, District & Session Judge (Retd.) as 
one man committee to re-determine the seniority of workers, who were working at FCI, Karnal. 


6 The Bajaj Committee submitted its report dated 05.07.2010 (Annexure W/7) which came under challenge in 
CWP. No.574/2011 and thereafter in LPA No.218 of 2011 titled as Girish Chandra Mahto and others Versus FCI, 
New Delhi and others. The aforesaid Bajaj Committee report was upheld by the Hon’ble Division Bench of High 
Court of Punjab & Haryana in the LPA No.218 of 2011 titled as Girish Chandra Mahto and others Versus FCI, 
New Delhi _and others vide order dated 20.03.2014 (Annexure W/8). In compliance of order dated 20.03.2014 
(Annexure W/8), all the workers except 38 workers appointed under the report/order dated 28.04.1994 made by Sh. R. 
K. Ranga were replaced by new incumbents. The aforesaid 38 workers were retained in employment by the FCI as 
they also found place in the seniority list of Bajaj Committee report. However, their date of birth/age as shown in the 
Bajaj Committee report is different from the date of birth/age as determined by the Chief Medical Officer (hereinafter 
called as CMO) at the time of their departmentalization. The union had demanded taking/accepting date of birth as per 
the certificate given by the CMO to the FCI not as per the date of birth as shown in seniority list of the Bajaj 
Committee Report. Out of aforesaid 38 workers, now 7 workers are being represented by the claimant union, who 
have filed the present claim. 


7. As per order dated 08.01.2009, the Bajaj Committee was entrusted with the job of determining the inter-se 
seniority of the workers of Karnal Depots only. The Bajaj Committee was never directed to determine the age of 
workers, nor was the said committee competent to do so. The Bajaj Committee mentioned in its report the date of 
birth of the workers as furnished by the concerned contractors. The Bajaj Committee had not called for the documents 
showing the proof of age as the same were not available to the contractors. In such circumstances, the workers should 
have been referred to the medical officers for the determination of their age through ossification test. 


8. The standing orders for the Industrial Establishments of the Food Corporation of India (Annexure W-11) 
applicable to the departmental workers of FCI vide clause 3(5) provides that proof of the date of birth of a workman is 
adducible from the relevant documents like matriculation certificate, school leaving certificate or the register 
maintained by the municipality in which date of birth is recorded, the register maintained by the registrar of births etc. 
and in the absence of such documents the medical certificate given by the Govt. Medical Officer is to be relied upon 
for the purpose of the age proof. The date of birth of a person cannot be made liable to be changed to the caprice of 
the respondent/management. 


9. The claimant union, by way of raising the instant industrial dispute, does not intend to challenge the Bajaj 
Committee Report, which has been upheld by the Hon’ble High Court of Punjab & Haryana and further by the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court and the issues as to the induction of the contract workers the under departmental labour

system in FCI, Karnal Complex have been put to rest after the implementation of the Bajaj Committee Report in 
compliance of the order dated 20.03.2014 passed by the LPA bench of the Hon’ble High Court of Punjab & Haryana. 
However, the workers, who were retained into employment vide appointment letter No. 
FCI/DO/KNL/Labour/Rectt./2011 dated 29.03.2011 (Annexure W/9) by the management as they found place in the 
seniority list of the Bajaj Committee Report also, are aggrieved by the non-consideration by the FCI of their date of

Complex and also as recorded in their service records like bio-data Form, Leave Travelling Concession (LTC)/ Bharat

10. Notice of the reference/claim was given to the respondent 10.1 & 2, who filed reply thereof maintaining 
therein that the issue regarding the date of birth recorded in the Bajaj Committee Report and relied upon by the FCI 
was disputed without appreciating the fact that the said report has already attained finality and no further interference 
is called for the order of the Hon’ble Court, which has attained finality up to the Hon’ble Supreme Court. The 
conciliation proceedings held on the issue could not materialize and failure report was sent by the authority. The 
reference made by the appropriate Government is totally wrong as the FCI has no power to change any content of the 
Bajaj Committee Report which has attained finality up to the Hon’ble Supreme Court and thereby the reference made 
to this Hon’ble Tribunal is totally irrelevant and uncalled for as the answer to the same is already contained in the 
judgment of the Hon’ble High Court (Annexure W/8) wherein the FCI has been directed to implement the Bajaj 
Committee Report in toto. For the purpose of identification and seniority of workers for departmentalization at the 
specified depots of FCI, the headquarters of FCI issued a circular containing certain guidelines. Numbers of 
committees were appointed for identification and determination of seniority of the contract workers for the food 
storage depot at Karnal as it is only at Karnal that claims and counter claims remains under agitation from one group 
of workers or the other. Otherwise, in the rest of the specified depots, the process of departmentalization of contract 
workers was smoothly carried out. 251 workers were to be departmentalized as per the requirement in the year 1991. 
However, as on today because of the drastic change in the policies of the Central Government, the said work has been 
shifted either to the State Agencies or through the private entrepreneurs and the FCI is rather facing the problem of 
surplus labour. In pursuance of Sh. R. K. Ranga, 251 contract workers were departmentalized at Karnal. 


11. The Hon’ble High Court of Punjab & Haryana while deciding CWP bearing No.11647 of 1994 titled_as 
Ram _Rattan_and_ others Versus Food Corporation of India and others quashed all actions based upon various 
committees, taken in the process of departmentalization and appointed a new one man committee of Sh. R. P. Bajaj, 
District & Session Judge (Retd.) to re-determine the seniority of the contract workers. Shri R. P. Bajaj submitted his 
report dated 05.07.2010 and determined various aspects including the date of birth of the contract workers which was 
also made basis to determine the seniority in the event of a set of workers were found to be having the same number 
of months of experience. Bajaj Committee Report was challenged by the workers up to Hon’ble Supreme Court and 
was upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court and thus has attained finality. In compliance of the directions issued by the 
Hon’ble High Court, contract workers up to Serial No. 251 of the seniority list finalized by the Bajaj Committee, were 
issued with the appointment letters in March, 2011 out of which 38 workers were those who were earlier also 
recommended to be departmentalized by the earlier Committees. So far as the date of birth mentioned in the seniority 
list by the Bajaj Committee is concerned, the same has to be treated as final in the absence of any challenge by the 
claimants and in view of the finality given to the said report upto the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India. The FCI has no 
jurisdiction to make any change in the contents of the Bajaj Committee Report and the seniority determined by the 
said Committee. The Bajaj Committee was required to determine each and every issue for departmentalization of 
contract workers at Karnal Depot which also includes the date of birth as in the case of many of the contract workers, 
the number of months of experience was the same, therefore, the date of birth was determined by the Bajaj Committee

Findings:- 

21. The dispute between the claimant union and respondents is regarding date of birth of workmen. As per 
respondents, date of birth as shown in the seniority list of Bajaj Committee report is legal. On the other hand, the case 


of the claimant union is this that the date of birth shown in the list of Bajaj Committee Report is illegal and it should 
have been taken as per seniority list MW1/WW1. 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : सितम्बर 27, 2025/आश्विन 5, 1947 6271 


22. In this regard, it is pertinent to mention here that as per own case of the claimant union on the basis of the 
report of Sh. R K Ranga dated 28.04.1994 under the directions of Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court, inter se 
seniority of the works of FCI, Karnal was fixed and 251 workers were departmentalized on regular vacancies. 
However, the report dated 28.04.1994 (Annexure W/16) of Sh. R. K. Ranga was challenged in CWP_bearing 
No.11647 of 1994 titled as Ram Rattan and others Versus Food Corporation of India and others before the Hon'ble 
High Court and the Hon'ble High Court vide order dated 08.01.2009 (Annexure W/6) quashed the report dated 
28.04.1994 of Sh. R. K. Ranga and appointed Sh. R. P. Bajaj as one man committee to re-determine the seniority of 
workers working with FCI, who submitted his report dated 05.07.2010, which was challenged in CWP No.574/2011 
and thereafter, in LPA No.218 of 2011 titled as Girish Chandra Mahto and others Versus FCI, New Delhi and 
others, it was upheld vide order dated 20.03.2014. In compliance of order dated 20.03.2014, all the workers except 38 
workers appointed under the report/order dated 28.04.1994 made by Sh. R. K. Ranga were replaced by new 
incumbents. The aforesaid 38 workers were retained in employment by the FCI as they also found place in the 
seniority list of Bajaj Committee report. However, their date of birth/age as shown in the Bajaj Committee report is 
different from the date of birth/age as determined by the CMO at the time of their departmentalization. The claimant 
union had demanded taking/accepting date of birth as per the certificate given by the CMO to the FCI not as per the 
date of birth as shown in seniority list of the Bajaj Committee Report. Out of aforesaid 38 workers, now 7 workers are 
being represented by the claimant union, who have filed the present claim. 


23. As per claimants, the Bajaj Committee has not called for the documents showing the proof of age as the 
same were not available to the contractors. In these circumstances, the workers should have been referred to the 
Medical officer for determination of their age through ossification test and as per Clause 3(5) of the standing order 
(Ex.W/11) also in the absence of such documents the medical certificate given by the Govt. Medical Officer is to be 
relied upon for the purpose of the age proof. The date of birth of a person cannot be made liable to be changed on the 
whims and fancies of the respondent/management. In this regard, it is pointed out that some workers have challenged 
their claim to enter their age in record as per medical certificate issued by CMO, which was rejected by the 
respondent in Jathu Rai case (supra), the relevant para nos.3 to 6, 10 & 11 are reproduced as under: 


3. The petitioners are working with respondents as Labourers. They were initially working with FCI through 
contractor. The Government of India as well as State of Haryana framed policy whereby it was decided that 
workers working through contractor would be departmentalized. The petitioners came to be departmentalized. 
The dispute arose with respect to their age and seniority. The matter was referred to different committees and 
ultimately this Court vide judgment dated 08.01.2009 in CWP No.11647 of 1994 titled as Ram Ratan and others 
vs. Food Corporation of India and others appointed Mr. R. P. Bajaj, District & Sessions Judge (Retd.) to 
resolve the issue. The relevant extracts of the judgment are reproduced as below : 


“18. For the reasons stated above, the report dated 29.4.1994 (Annexure P-1) submitted by Shri R. K. Ranga, 
cannot be said to be in accordance with the directions issued by this Court and, therefore, cannot be sustained 
and is hereby quashed and accordingly, this writ petition is allowed. 19. The matter has been lingering since 
long and the petitioners are waiting for the determination of their seniority on the basis of which their rights 
would be crystalized. This position cannot be allowed to be kept pending for all times to come and even the 
Division Bench of this Court while deciding LPA No.319 of 1998 and L.P.A.No.350 of 1998 had indicated that 
the matter needs to be resolved. Keeping the same in view and in the light of the fact that this writ petition has 
been pending in this Court since 1994, it would be appropriate that Shri R. P. Bajaj, District & Sessions Judge 
(Retd.), H.No.5460, Sector 38 (West), Chandigarh, be appointed as a one man Committee to examine all the 
relevant records produced before the Chopra Committee and the report of the Ranga Committee in the light of 
the directions of this Court in its orders dated 21.9.1993 and 4.2.1994 and then to redetermine the seniority of 
the workers who were working at FCI Karnal Depot. Let the said exercise be completed within a period of four 
months from today. Appropriate steps in accordance with law will be taken in pursuance to the seniority fixed 
by Shri R. P. Bajaj, within a period of one month thereafter.” 


4. Mr. Bajaj, considering different reports, issues involved and representation of stakeholders prepared 
seniority list of 542 workers. In the report, the date of birth of the workers was noticed apart from months of 
their experience. The said report came to be challenged before this Court by way of CWP No.574 of 2011. This 
Court vide order dated 13.01.2011 upheld report of Mr. Bajaj’s Committee and dismissed the writ petition. The 
relevant extracts of the order dated 13.01.2011 are reproduced as below: 


“The main submission, as made, is that Bajaj Committee has gone outside the purview of direction issued by 
Single Judge and had not taken into consideration the reports of all the Committees, as per direction given in 
the order as well as by the LPA Bench. 


Tam unable to accept the submission made by learned counsel for the petitioners. The Bajaj Committee report, 
which is annexed with the petition as Annexure P-7, is comprehensive, giving history of the issues involved and 
various Committees that had earlier gone into to examine the issue. Reference is made to the reports of Dalela 
Committee, Chopra Committee and the Ranga Committee as well and thereafter it is concluded that in depth 
study of reports of all the four Committees set up by the Food Corporation of India to determine seniority, the 


6272 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA :SEPTEMBER 27, 2025/ASVINA 5, 1947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


Chopra Committee report is found unblemished. This report was found to be well reasoned and to be in 
conformity with the parameters laid down in the F.C.I circulars issued in the year 1991. The finding also is that 
this will lessen the agony of those persons who were deprived of the benefit of seniority as given by Chopra 
Committee report due to undue benefit given on the basis of Ranga Committee report, which had been quashed 
it, thus, cannot be said that Bajaj Committee has in any manner gone outside the purview or parameters laid 
down by learned Single Judge of this Court. Once after detailed analysis, the Bajaj Committee has come to 
conclude that Chopra Committee has reached the correct conclusion, then it can be observed that mode and 
method adopted by the Bajaj Committee was fair, just and equitable and would not suffer from any infirmity as 
urged by counsel for the petitioners. 


The fact that some evidence regarding gate register was not produced before the Bajaj Committee would also 
not mean much as same registers were not found available but the names of those employees, reflected in these 
registers were taken from Chopra Committee report before which these registers had been earlier produced. It 
can not, therefore, be said that the Bajaj Committee report would be bad on the ground that relevant material 
was not considered and that it would call for interference in exercise of writ jurisdiction by this Court. 


The submission that the matter be referred to the Labour Court for determination would be too late in a day to 
accept and such submission, if any, ought to have been made before the Single Judge or the LPA Bench, where 
this plea was never raised. The order passed by the learned Single Judge in CWP No.11647 of 1994 and that 
passed by the LPA Bench was allowed to acquire finality and was not put to any challenge, cannot be allowed 
to be now challenged in under hand manner by challenging the report of Bajaj Committee with a prayer to refer 
the matter for examination by Labour Court. There is, thus, no merit in the writ petition and the same is 
accordingly dismissed.” 


5. The aggrieved parties preferred intra-court appeal which came up for consideration before a Division Bench 
of this Court. The Appellate Court vide judgment dated 20.03.2014 dismissed appeal and upheld judgment of 
Single Judge. The Appellate Court further directed FCI to implement the report submitted by Mr. Bajaj 
Committee in toto. The relevant extracts of the judgment are reproduced as below : 


“Learned Single Judge has discussed each and every aspect and has rightly come to the conclusion that Mr. 
Bajaj has discussed reports made by all the Committees and further looked into record produced before him 
and written submissions made by the parties concerned. Perusal of the report indicates that the proceedings 
continued on many dates and the opportunities of hearing and to place on record the documents were granted 
to all the concerned parties. It is not in dispute that the appellants in this case are in service on account of the 
report made by Mr. Ranga in the year 1994. That report was rejected by this Court as has been referred to 
above. Accordingly, on the basis of the report made by Mr. Ranga, the appellants do not have any right to 
remain in service. However, they are continuing as such by making determined effort to keep the litigation 
alive. Despite relieving orders issued, they are continuing in service under the order passed by this Court from 
time to time. At one point of time, stay application filed by them was dismissed. They went to Hon'ble Supreme 
Court by filing SLP, which was also dismissed. 


In view of the above, we are of the opinion that the order passed by learned Single Judge is perfectly justified. 
The appeal is accordingly dismissed. 


However, the FCT is directed to implement the report submitted by Mr. Bajaj in toto. It is made clear that all the 
appellants and others, who were given appointments, in terms of the report made by Mr. Ranga leave their 
assignment within 15 days from today. The authorities of the FCI may adjust the appellants if the vacancy exists 
subject to their moving applications and their applications will be considered strictly in terms of the seniority 
list as per the report made by Mr. Bajaj Needful shall be done within four months and if the claim of the 
appellants is rejected, it will not furnish a cause for them to agitate the matter any further.” 


6. The aggrieved persons further unsuccessfully preferred SLP before Supreme Court. 


10. The conceded position emerging from record is that the petitioners were initially working with FCI through 
contractor. They came to be departmentalized in view of instructions issued by Government of India. They were 
not having concrete evidence of their age, thus, different mode and methods were adopted to ascertain their 
age. This Court appointed Mr. Bajaj to determine seniority of petitioners. Mr. Bajaj in_ his report has noted 


date of birth of petitioners and thereafter, on the basis of age and experience, has determined seniority. 


11. It is undisputed fact that Bajaj committee in its report has jotted down date of birth of all the petitioners. 


They are not assailing report of Bajaj Committee. In any case, said report has been upheld by this Court and 


SLP against judgment of a Division Bench of this Court stands dismissed. The petitioners are claiming that 


their age should be determined on the basis of medical report instead of report of Bajaj Committee. The 


medical report indicates age of petitioners with margin of 4/5 years. It is a settled proposition of law that 


medical report especially ossification test is a corroborative evidence and it does not conclusively prove age of 


any person. The evidence of medical report, thus, is not a conclusive evidence. Mr. Bajaj in his report has 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : सितम्बर 27, 2025/आश्विन 5, 1947 6273 


noted date of birth of all the petitioners. They have not challenged said report rather said report has already 
been upheld by this Court. 


24. A perusal of aforesaid paras made it ample clear, specifically para 11 mentioned above, that R. P. Bajaj 
Committee had considered the date of birth of the workers and has given its findings accordingly. Now claimant 
union again raised this dispute before this Tribunal as the matter has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court 


and the LPA No.2543/2024 titled as Dilip Kumar and others versus Food Corporation of India and others thereof 


was also dismissed, wherein in para no.4, it is held as under:- 


“4. The appellants are stated to be working as ‘Palledar’ (Handling Worker) through a Contractor. They had sought 
absorption in the department and a Committee headed by Sh. R.P. Bajaj, retired District and Sessions Judge had been 
constituted to determine the age and the seniority of the workers. The Bajaj Committee in its report dated 05.07.2010 
had determined the seniority of the workers wherein the age and date of birth had been specifically mentioned. The 
report of the Bajaj Committee was challenged by some of the workers by preferring CWP No.23481 of 2014 which 
was dismissed. The LPA No.218 of 2011 thereagainst was also dismissed. The Special Leave Petition thereagainst 
was also dismissed.” 


25. When findings of the Hon'ble High Court have come regarding age of the workman, this Tribunal cannot re- 
determine the date of birth of the workers specially on the basis of the medical opinion as mentioned in Jathu Rai 
case (supra), the evidence of medical report is not conclusive evidence. To support this view, reliance can be placed 
on Criminal Appeal Nos.1119-1120 of 2016 titled as Mukarrab etc. versus State of U. P. decided by the Hon'ble 
Supreme Court of India. 


26. It is added here that so far as this argument of the ld. counsel for the claimant union that workers were not 
party in the Jathu Rai Case (supra), the same is devoid of merit as the case was filed by some of the co-workers, 
whose date of birth was determined by the Bajaj Committee and it was upheld by the Hon'ble High Court. 


27. So far as this argument of the Id. counsel for the claimant union that due to findings given in LPA 
No.2543/2024 titled as Dilip Kumar and others versus Food Corporation of India and others, the findings in Jathu 
Rai_case (supra), cannot be relied upon. In this regard, it is pointed out that Hon'ble High Court in ELPA 
No.2543/2024 titled as Dilip Kumar _and_ others versus Food Corporation of India and others has upheld the 
decision of the Jathu Rai case (supra) and it does not lie in the mouth of the claimant union that findings of Jathu 
Rai case (supra) has become irrelevant. Rather in LPA No.2543/2024 titled as Dilip Kumar and others versus Food 


Corporation of India and others, the findings given in Jathu Rai case (supra) have been upheld and thus have been 
authenticated by the Hon'ble High Court. 


28. So far as standing order is concerned, the same is undoubtedly issued by the FCI. However, the standing 
order is not having force, specifically when the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukarrab etc. versus State of U. P. 
(supra), has held that medical evidence is not conclusive evidence. Keeping in view the fact that medical opinion is 
not conclusive evidence. No reliance can be placed on the plea of the claimant union that on the basis of the medical 
evidence, their age should be determined. It is also pointed out that Hon'ble High Court in Jathu Rai case (supra) has 
categorically held that Mr. Bajaj in his report has noted date of birth of petitioners and thereafter, on the basis of age 
and experience, has determined seniority. 


29. So far as case titled as M/s Agra Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. v/s Workman (supra) is concerned, the same is 


not relevant for decision of this case. 


30. The claim being devoid of merit is dismissed. The reference is answered accordingly.

Central Government vide Notification No.L-22011/14/2015-IR(CM-II) dated 31.08.2015, under sub-section 
(1) and sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (hereinafter called the Act), has referred 
the following Industrial dispute for adjudication to this Tribunal:- 


“Whether the action of the management of Food Corporation of India taking the date of birth of 
workman Shri Janki Shahni as shown in the seniority list of the Bajaj Committee Report is legal and 
justified? If not, what relief the workman is entitled and from which date?” 


1. Brief facts of the case as per claim statement filed on behalf of workman are that the claimant was appointed 
by the management of Food Corporation of India (hereinafter called as FCT) on 03.05.1994 for working in FCI Karnal 
as A/labour. He had been working upto 30.04.2014 with the respondent no.1 continuously as A/labour and the work 
and conduct of the claimant remained good and satisfactory during the course of his service with the respondent 10.1. 
The services of the claimant were dispensed with on 30.04.2014 without following the procedure laid down in the Act 
as well as in the model standing order. The claimant has completed more than 240 days continuously as required 
under the Act, so he was entitled to the protection under Sections 25F, 25G and 25H of the Act, which the 
respondents has not followed. At the time of joining, the respondent got conducted medical examination of the 
workman and as per the medical certificate, age of the claimant was 34 years but the respondents had treated his age 
as 39 years and the respondents wrongly incorporated the date of birth of the claimant as 21.09.1955, which was 
mentioned in all service record i.e. appointment letter, CFP Slip, Pay Slip, Declaration Letter, Pan Card and Identity 
Card etc. 


2: The respondents have terminated the services of the claimant without considering the actual age of the 
workman. As per the date of birth shown in the service record, the claimant got the retirement on 30.09.2015 but the 
respondents has terminated the services on 30.04.2014, which is immature and against the principle of natural justice 
and against the provisions of the Act. 


3. The standing orders for the Industrial Establishments of the Food Corporation of India applicable to the 
departmental workers of FCI vide clause 3(5) provides that proof of the date of birth of a workman is adducible from 
the relevant documents like matriculation certificate, school leaving certificate or the register maintained by the 
municipality in which date of birth is recorded, the register maintained by the registrar of births etc. and in the 
absence of such documents the medical certificate given by the Govt. Medical Officer is to be relied upon for the 
purpose of the age proof. The date of birth of a person cannot be made liable to be changed to the caprice of the 
respondent/management. Clause 4 of the standing order provides for age of retirement as 60 years, but the 
respondents has totally ignored the said standing order and made premature termination of the claimant.

Findings:- 

20. The sole dispute between the parties is this whether the action of the management of Food Corporation of 
India in taking the date of birth of workman as shown in the seniority list of the Bajaj Committee Report is legal and 
justified or it should have been taken as per medical certificate Ex. WW 1/2, wherein it has been mentioned that at the 
time of entry into service, the age of the claimant was 34 yers. It is pertinent to mention here that in the service record, 
date of birth of the claimant is 21.09.1955, however, Bajaj Committee has determined his date of birth as 10.04.1954. 
However, as per affidavit, his actual date of birth is 21.09.1951. Thus there are three date of births of the claimant, 
which are as follows:- 


1. as per service record:-21.09.1955 
j. as per Bajaj Committee Report:- 10.04.1954 
k. as per affidavit of claimant:-21.09.1951.

21. In this regard, it is pertinent to mention here that as per own case of the claimant on the basis of the report of 
Sh. R K Ranga dated 28.04.1994 under the directions of Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court, inter se seniority of 
the works of FCI, Karnal was fixed and 251 workers were departmentalized on regular vacancies. However, the report 


dated 28.04.1994 of Sh. R. K. Ranga was challenged in CWP bearing No.11647 of 1994 titled as Ram Rattan and 


others Versus Food Corporation of India and others before the Hon'ble High Court and the Hon'ble High Court vide 
order dated 08.01.2009 (MW-1) quashed the report dated 28.04.1994 of Sh. R. K. Ranga and appointed Sh. R. P. 


Bajaj as one man committee to re-determine the seniority of workers working with FCI, who submitted his report 
dated 05.07.2010 (Ex.WW1/5), which was challenged in CWP No.574/2011 and thereafter, in ELPA No.218 of 2011 
titled as Girish Chandra Mahto and others Versus FCI, New Delhi_and others, it was upheld vide order dated 
20.03.2014 (Ex.MW-1). In compliance of order dated 20.03.2014 (Ex.MW-3), all the workers except 38 workers 
appointed under the report/order dated 28.04.1994 made by Sh. R. K. Ranga were replaced by new incumbents. The 
aforesaid 38 workers were retained in employment by the FCI as they also found place in the seniority list of Bajaj 
Committee report. However, their date of birth/age as shown in the Bajaj Committee report is different from the date 
of birth/age as determined by the CMO at the time of their departmentalization. The claimant had demanded 
taking/accepting date of birth as per the certificate given by the CMO to the FCI not as per the date of birth as shown 
in seniority list of the Bajaj Committee Report. Out of aforesaid 38 workers, the claimant Sh. Janki Sahni has filed the 
present claim. 


22. As per claimant, the Bajaj Committee has not called for the documents showing the proof of age as the same 
were not available to the contractors. In these circumstances, the workers should have been referred to the Medical 
officer for determination of their age through ossification test and as per Clause 3(5) of the standing order 
(Ex.WW 1/4) also in the absence of such documents the medical certificate given by the Govt. Medical Officer is to be 
relied upon for the purpose of the age proof. The date of birth of a person cannot be made liable to be changed on the 
whims and fancies of the respondents/management. In this regard, it is pointed out that some workers have challenged 
their claim to enter their age in record as per medical certificate issued by CMO, which was rejected by the 


respondent in Jathu Rai case (supra) bearing CWP_No.23481 of 2014, the relevant para nos.3 to 6, 10 & 11 are 


reproduced as under: 


3. The petitioners are working with respondents as Labourers. They were initially working with FCI through 
contractor. The Government of India as well as State of Haryana framed policy whereby it was decided that 
workers working through contractor would be departmentalized. The petitioners came to be departmentalized. 
The dispute arose with respect to their age and seniority. The matter was referred to different committees and 
ultimately this Court vide judgment dated 08.01.2009 in CWP No.11647 of 1994 titled as Ram Ratan and others 
vs. Food Corporation of India and others appointed Mr. R.P.Bajaj, District & Sessions Judge (Retd.) to resolve 
the issue. The relevant extracts of the judgment are reproduced as below : 


“18. For the reasons stated above, the report dated 29.4.1994 (Annexure P-1) submitted by Shri R.K.Ranga, 
cannot be said to be in accordance with the directions issued by this Court and, therefore, cannot be sustained 
and is hereby quashed and accordingly, this writ petition is allowed. 19. The matter has been lingering since 
long and the petitioners are waiting for the determination of their seniority on the basis of which their rights 
would be crystalized. This position cannot be allowed to be kept pending for all times to come and even the 
Division Bench of this Court while deciding LPA No.319 of 1998 and L.P.A.No.350 of 1998 had indicated that 
the matter needs to be resolved. Keeping the same in view and in the light of the fact that this writ petition has 
been pending in this Court since 1994, it would be appropriate that Shri R.P.Bajaj, District & Sessions Judge 
(Retd.), H.No.5460, Sector 38 (West), Chandigarh, be appointed as a one man Committee to examine all the 
relevant records produced before the Chopra Committee and the report of the Ranga Committee in the light of 
the directions of this Court in its orders dated 21.9.1993 and 4.2.1994 and then to redetermine the seniority of 
the workers who were working at FCI Karnal Depot. Let the said exercise be completed within a period of four 
months from today. Appropriate steps in accordance with law will be taken in pursuance to the seniority fixed 
by Shri R.P.Bajaj, within a period of one month thereafter.” 


4. Mr. Bajaj, considering different reports, issues involved and representation of stakeholders prepared 
seniority list of 542 workers. In the report, the date of birth of the workers was noticed apart from months of 
their experience. The said report came to be challenged before this Court by way of CWP No.574 of 2011. This 
Court vide order dated 13.01.2011 upheld report of Mr. Bajaj’s Committee and dismissed the writ petition. The 
relevant extracts of the order dated 13.01.2011 are reproduced as below: 


“The main submission, as made, is that Bajaj Committee has gone outside the purview of direction issued by 
Single Judge and had not taken into consideration the reports of all the Committees, as per direction given in 
the order as well as by the LPA Bench. 


Tam unable to accept the submission made by learned counsel for the petitioners. The Bajaj Committee report, 
which is annexed with the petition as Annexure P-7, is comprehensive, giving history of the issues involved and 
various Committees that had earlier gone into to examine the issue. Reference is made to the reports of Dalela 
Committee, Chopra Committee and the Ranga Committee as well and thereafter it is concluded that in depth

study of reports of all the four Committees set up by the Food Corporation of India to determine seniority, the 
Chopra Committee report is found unblemished. This report was found to be well reasoned and to be in 
conformity with the parameters laid down in the F.C.I circulars issued in the year 1991. The finding also is that 
this will lessen the agony of those persons who were deprived of the benefit of seniority as given by Chopra 
Committee report due to undue benefit given on the basis of Ranga Committee report, which had been quashed 
it, thus, cannot be said that Bajaj Committee has in any manner gone outside the purview or parameters laid 
down by learned Single Judge of this Court. Once after detailed analysis, the Bajaj Committee has come to 
conclude that Chopra Committee has reached the correct conclusion, then it can be observed that mode and 
method adopted by the Bajaj Committee was fair, just and equitable and would not suffer from any infirmity as 
urged by counsel for the petitioners. 


The fact that some evidence regarding gate register was not produced before the Bajaj Committee would also 
not mean much as same registers were not found available but the names of those employees, reflected in these 
registers were taken from Chopra Committee report before which these registers had been earlier produced. It 
cannot, therefore, be said that the Bajaj Committee report would be bad on the ground that relevant material 
was not considered and that it would call for interference in exercise of writ jurisdiction by this Court. 


The submission that the matter be referred to the Labour Court for determination would be too late in a day to 
accept and such submission, if any, ought to have been made before the Single Judge or the LPA Bench, where 
this plea was never raised. The order passed by the learned Single Judge in CWP No.11647 of 1994 and that 
passed by the LPA Bench was allowed to acquire finality and was not put to any challenge, cannot be allowed 
to be now challenged in under hand manner by challenging the report of Bajaj Committee with a prayer to refer 
the matter for examination by Labour Court. There is, thus, no merit in the writ petition and the same is 
accordingly dismissed.” 


5. The aggrieved parties preferred intra-court appeal which came up for consideration before a Division Bench 
of this Court. The Appellate Court vide judgment dated 20.03.2014 dismissed appeal and upheld judgment of 
Single Judge. The Appellate Court further directed FCI to implement the report submitted by Mr. Bajaj 
Committee in toto. The relevant extracts of the judgment are reproduced as below:- 


“Learned Single Judge has discussed each and every aspect and has rightly come to the conclusion that Mr. 
Bajaj has discussed reports made by all the Committees and further looked into record produced before him 
and written submissions made by the parties concerned. Perusal of the report indicates that the proceedings 
continued on many dates and the opportunities of hearing and to place on record the documents were granted 
to all the concerned parties. It is not in dispute that the appellants in this case are in service on account of the 
report made by Mr. Ranga in the year 1994. That report was rejected by this Court as has been referred to 
above. Accordingly, on the basis of the report made by Mr. Ranga, the appellants do not have any right to 
remain in service. However, they are continuing as such by making determined effort to keep the litigation 
alive. Despite relieving orders issued, they are continuing in service under the order passed by this Court from 
time to time. At one point of time, stay application filed by them was dismissed. They went to Hon'ble Supreme 
Court by filing SLP, which was also dismissed. 


In view of the above, we are of the opinion that the order passed by learned Single Judge is perfectly justified. 
The appeal is accordingly dismissed. 


However, the FCT is directed to implement the report submitted by Mr. Bajaj in toto. It is made clear that all the 
appellants and others, who were given appointments, in terms of the report made by Mr. Ranga leave their 
assignment within 15 days from today. The authorities of the FCI may adjust the appellants if the vacancy exists 
subject to their moving applications and their applications will be considered strictly in terms of the seniority 
list as per the report made by Mr. Bajaj Needful shall be done within four months and if the claim of the 
appellants is rejected, it will not furnish a cause for them to agitate the matter any further.” 


6. The aggrieved persons further unsuccessfully preferred SLP before Supreme Court. 


10. The conceded position emerging from record is that the petitioners were initially working with FCI through 
contractor. They came to be departmentalized in view of instructions issued by Government of India. They were 
not having concrete evidence of their age, thus, different mode and methods were adopted to ascertain their 
age. This Court appointed Mr. Bajaj to determine seniority of petitioners. Mr. Bajaj in his report has noted 


date of birth of petitioners and thereafter, on the basis of age and experience, has determined seniority. 


11. It is undisputed fact that Bajaj committee in its report has jotted down date of birth of all the petitioners. 


They are not assailing report of Bajaj Committee. In any case, said report has been upheld by this Court and 


SLP against judgment of a Division Bench of this Court stands dismissed. The petitioners are claiming that 


their age should be determined on the basis of medical report instead of report of Bajaj Committee. The 


medical report indicates age of petitioners with margin of 4/5 years. It is a settled proposition of law that 


medical report especially ossification test is a corroborative evidence and it does not conclusively prove age of

any person. The evidence of medical report, thus, is not a conclusive evidence. Mr. Bajaj in his report has 


noted date of birth of all the petitioners. They have not challenged said report rather said report has already 
been upheld by this Court. 


23. A perusal of aforesaid paras made it ample clear, specifically para 11 mentioned above, that R. P. Bajaj 
Committee had considered the date of birth of the workers and has given its findings accordingly. Now claimant again 
raised this dispute before this Tribunal as the matter has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court and the EPA 
No.2543/2024 titled as Dilip Kumar and others versus Food Corporation of India and others thereof was also 


dismissed, wherein in para no.4, it is held as under:- 


“4. The appellants are stated to be working as ‘Palledar’ (Handling Worker) through a Contractor. They had sought 
absorption in the department and a Committee headed by Sh. R.P. Bajaj, retired District and Sessions Judge had been 
constituted to determine the age and the seniority of the workers. The Bajaj Committee in its report dated 05.07.2010 
had determined the seniority of the workers wherein the age and date of birth had been specifically mentioned. The 
report of the Bajaj Committee was challenged by some of the workers by preferring CWP No.23481 of 2014 which 
was dismissed. The LPA No.218 of 2011 thereagainst was also dismissed. The Special Leave Petition thereagainst 
was also dismissed.” 


24. When findings of the Hon'ble High Court have come regarding age of the workman, this Tribunal cannot re- 
determine the date of birth of the workman specially on the basis of the medical opinion as mentioned in Jathu Rai 
case (supra), the evidence of medical report is not conclusive evidence. To support this view, reliance can be placed 
on Criminal Appeal Nos.1119-1120 of 2016 titled as Mukarrab etc. versus State of U. P. decided by the Hon'ble 
Supreme Court of India. 


25. It is added here that so far as this argument of the ld. counsel for the claimant that workers were not party in 
the Jathu Rai Case (supra), the same is devoid of merit as the case was filed by some of the co-workers, whose date 
of birth was determined by the Bajaj Committee and it was upheld by the Hon'ble High Court. 


26. So far as this argument of the Id. counsel for the claimant that due to findings given in LPA No.2543/2024 
titled as Dilip Kumar and others versus Food Corporation of India and others, the findings in Jathu Rai case (supra), 
cannot be relied upon. Rather, Hon'ble High Court in LPA No.2543/2024 titled as Dilip Kumar and others versus 
Food Corporation of India and others has upheld the decision of the Jathu Rai case (supra) and it does not lie in the 
mouth of the claimant that findings of Jathu Rai case (supra) has become irrelevant. 


27. So far as standing order is concerned, the same is undoubtedly issued by the FCI. However, the standing 
order is not having force, specifically when the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Criminal Appeal Nos.1119-1120 of 2016 
titled as Mukarrab etc. versus State of U.P. has held that medical evidence is not conclusive evidence. Keeping in 
view the fact that medical opinion is not conclusive evidence. No reliance can be placed on the plea of the claimant 
that on the basis of the medical evidence, their age should be determined. It is also pointed out that Hon'ble High 
Court in Jathu Rai case (supra) has categorically held that Mr. Bajaj in his report has noted date of birth of claimant 
and thereafter, on the basis of age and experience, has determined seniority. 


28. As per Bajaj Committee Report, the date of birth of the claimant is 10.04.1954 and he has been retired on 
30.04.2014 on attaining the age of superannuation of 60 years. There was no necessity of compliance of Section 25F 
of the Act, so there was no violation of any of the provisions of the Act. The claim being devoid of merit is dismissed. 
The reference is answered accordingly. 


29. Let copy of this award be sent to the Appropriate Government as required under Section 17 of the Act for 
publication.

AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-22012/4/2019-IR(CM-ID) dated 13/02/2019 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Patmohona Colliery, Sodepur Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and their 
workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the Management of M/s Eastern Coalfields Ltd. in relation to its Patmohana Colliery 
under Sodepur Area in not considering promotion in respect of Sri Prakash Chandra Panda from Trammer 
Cat-III to Looseman Cat-IV w.e.f. 01-11-2011 along with consequential benefits is just and legal? If not, to 
what relief the workman is entitled to?” 


1 On receiving Order No. L-22012/4/2019-IR(CM-ID) dated 13/02/2019 from the Government of India 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case No. 14 of 2019 was registered on 
06/03/2019 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear 
and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. Koyala Mazdoor Congress filed written statement on behalf of the aggrieved workman on 11/11/2022. 
Management contested the Industrial Dispute by filing their written statement on 01/02/2023. Fact of the union’s case 
in brief is that Prakash Chandra Panda was posted at Patmohona Colliery and was earlier regularized from PR UG 
Loader Group V-A to Timber Mazdoor, Cat-II on 02/05/2003 as a ‘Time Rated’ worker. During fixation of his pay in 
Time Rated category he was not granted any pay protection due to which he faced huge monetary loss to the extent of 
Rs. 69.83 per day. He was again regularized as Underground Trammer, Cat-III in the year 2006. In the year 2011, 
Prakash Chandra Panda was regularized to the post of Looseman, Cat-IV from the post of Underground Trammer, 
Cat-HI instead of granting promotional benefit. According to the union, the stand taken by the management is totally 
wrong and illegal as the aggrieved workman has only been regularized from Cat-III to Cat-IV. He is entitled to get 
promotional benefit with one increment in his basic pay. Union prayed for providing direction upon the management 
of Patmohona Colliery, Sodepur Area to consider the case of Prakash Chandra Panda and grant him fitment of basic 
wages with pay protection from UG Loader to Timber Mazdoor and also give promotional benefit from UG Trammer 
Cat-III to Looseman, Cat-IV. 


3. Management of ECL in written statement has claimed that the dispute raised on behalf of Prakash Chandra 
Panda is misconceived and the Industrial Dispute referred by the appropriate government is not maintainable. It is the 
case of the management that the workman was converted from ‘Piece Rated’ UG Loader to the post of Timber 


6282 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA :SEPTEMBER 27, 2025/ASVINA 5, 1947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


Mazdoor in the year 2003 and was paid his wages due to him as per his entitlement. Union raised the Industrial 
Dispute in the year 2018, after fifteen years from the date of conversion and during this period four wage agreements 
of Coal India Limited were implemented. According to the management, workman is not entitled to get promotional 
benefit from Trammer Cat-III to Looseman, Cat-IV as both designations i.e. Trammer, Cat-II and Looseman, Cat-IV 
are in the same cadre and Sri Panda was regularized in the same cadre therefore, claim of union for giving benefits of 
promotion from Timber Mazdoor to Trammer in the year 2006 is not maintainable. It is asserted that management is 
justified in not giving one incremental benefit of promotion from Trammer to Looseman from the year 2011 and the 
concerned workman is not entitled to any relief. 


4. Prakash Chandra Panda has been examined as Workman Witness-I. In his affidavit-in-chief the workman 
stated that he was regularized from UG Trammer, Cat-HI to Looseman, Cat-IV in the year 2011 without granting him 
promotional benefits. It is further stated that regularization from Cat-III to Cat-IV is wrong and he is entitled to get 
promotional benefit by getting one incremental benefit with protection of basic pay. Documents produced by him 
have been admitted in evidence as follows: 


(i) copy of office order dated 02/05/2003 by which the workman was regularized as Timber Mazdoor is marked 
as Exhibit W-1. 


(ii) copies of pay statement for May, 2003 and June, 2003 are collectively marked as Exhibit W-2. 


(ili) copies of pay slips issued in his favour showing fixation of pay in July, 2006 and pay received by him in 
August, 2006 are collectively marked as Exhibit W-3. 


(iv) copies of pay slips showing that no promotional benefit was given on regularization to the post of Looseman, 
Catgory-IV is marked as Exhibit W-4. 


(v) copies of application and reminder submitted on 18/02/2012 and 04/08/2012 respectively to the Senior 
Manager, Patmohona Colliery for granting him promotional increment are marked as Exhibit W-5 and W-6 
respectively. 


During cross-examination witness deposed that he did not have any fixed pay at the time he worked as a UG 
Loader, Group V-A. He denied the suggestion that he is not entitled to any protection at the time of pay fixation 
during regularization to the post of Timber Mazdoor, Category-II. He also denied that there is no provision for 
payment of any promotional or incremental benefit on regularization of an employee from UG Trammer, Catgory-HI 
to Looseman, Catgory-IV. 


5. Mayuri Kar Verma, Asst. Manager (P) at Patmohona Colliery, Sodepur Area, ECL has deposed as 
Management Witness-I. In her examination-in-chief the witness stated that union’s claim that Sri Panda is entitled to 
get promotional benefit on his regularization from Trammer, Cat-III to Looseman, Cat-IV is wrong as both 
designations are in the same cadre. According to the MW-I, action of the management is proper and justified in not 
granting incremental benefit in the same cadre. In course of examination, witness produced the following documents: - 


(i) Copy of office order dated 25/07/2006 whereby some employees of Patmohona Colliery were regularized to 
different posts and categories is marked as Exhibit M-1 


(ii) Copy of office order dated 23/12/2011 by which basic wage of Prakash Chandra Panda, UG Trammer was 
fixed on his regularization from Trammer to Looseman w.e.f. 01/11/2011 is marked as Exhibits M-2. 


In cross-examination, witness deposed that Prakash Chandra Panda was not entitled to promotional benefits 
on his joining as Looseman from Trammer, Cat-III. Witness stated that in the present case there was no Notification 
for promotion. General Rule is that a person is converted to different post, his Service Linked Promotion is counted 
from the converted post and not from the original post. Witness denied that management committed any illegality by 
not providing promotional benefits to the workman on his posting as Looseman, Cat-IV. 


6. On a perusal of schedule, it appears that the dispute which needs to be adjudicated is whether posting of 
Prakash Chandra Panda from Trammer, Cat-III to Looseman, Cat-IV w.e.f. 01/11/2011 should be treated as 
promotion or regularization. It is apposite to note that in the present reference appropriate government has not raised 
the issue of regularization of Prakash Chandra Panda from PR UG Loader to the post of Timber Mazdoor, Cat-II in 
Time Rated category. Therefore, question which has been raised in Paragraph one of the union’s written statement, 
needs no consideration at this stage. 


7. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative advancing his argument for the workman submitted that by order 
dated 23/12/2011 (Exhibit M-2) it was provided that UG Trammers were posted as Looseman at Patmohona Colliery 
w.e.f. 01/11/2011 as per recommendation of the Departmental Promotion Committee which took into consideration 
the Manpower Budget and vacancy arising in these posts. Mr. Kumar referred to guiding principle for promotion of 
employees provided in Implementation Instruction No. 34 under NCWA-VI. Taking me through the contents of 
Annexure-XXVII-7 of Implementation Instruction No. 34, Mr. Kumar argued that promotion channel for Tramming 
personnels has been laid down and it is clearly provided that for posting as Tramming Personnels in Cat-HI mode of 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : सितम्बर 27, 2025/आश्विन 5, 1947 6283 


selection was followed and for the purpose of posting to Tramming Personnels Cat-IV, eligibility criteria was that the 
person should serve for four years in Cat-III and promotion would be held as per recommendation of Departmental 
Promotion Committee. Mr. Kumar ascertained that Prakash Chandra Panda, the aggrieved workman has not been 
granted promotional benefits of one increment in his pay @ three percent of basic pay. It is vehemently argued that a 
person moving upwards from Cat-III to Cat-[V on recommendation being made by Departmental Promotion 
Committee on considering Manpower Budget and vacancy arising in the post, posting in Cat-IV should be treated as 
promotion and not regularization. 


8. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate in reply argued that Looseman, Cat-IV is to be considered in Trammer 
category and for posting from Category-III to Cat-IV in the same cadre only amounts to regularization and not 
promotion. It is urged that the workman remained in the same cadre and he is not entitled to promotional benefits. 


9. Having considered rival contentions and arguments advanced, it appears to me that Prakash Chandra Panda 
who was posted as Trammer, Cat-II at Patmohona Colliery, Sodepur Area was posted as Looseman, Cat-IV. From 
the appended notes in Annexure-XXVII-7 it may be gathered that persons posted as Pointsman, Banksman, clipman, 
Coupler/Signalman, Setrider, Setman and Looseman who are in Cat-IV would grow as per the cadre scheme beyond 
category-IV. It implies that persons designated under various posts mentioned above are included in the group of 
Tramming personnels. Chart provided in Implementation Instruction No. 34 reveals that mode of selection or 
promotion from Trammer, (गा to Trammer, Cat-[V would be on recommendation of Departmental Promotion 
Committee and the same provides for promotional channel for Tramming personnels. It can therefore be assumed that 
a person moving upwards in channel from Tramming personnels, Cat-III to Tramming Personnels, Cat-[V/Looseman, 
Cat-IV is a promotion effected on the recommendation of Departmental Promotion Committee and such posting to a 
higher category cannot be termed as regularization. In my considered opinion the concerned workman appearing 
against serial No. ten (10) of Exhibit M-1 has not been provided with any increment in his basic pay while fixing his 
pay, which usually accompanies a promotion. Since posting to a higher category is a promotion of an employee, he is 
entitled to receive promotional benefits by way of grant of increment @ three percent of basic pay. Therefore, the 
aggrieved workman is entitled to a promotional benefit of three percent of basic pay w.e.f. 01/11/2011. Management 
of the company is directed to pay arrears of incremental benefits which accrued to Prakash Chandra Panda from 
01/11/2011. I further hold that the management of ECL acted in an arbitrary and illegal manner by not granting 
promotional benefits to the incumbent and by fixing pay without change of any basic by treating such change of 
designation as regularization instead of promotion. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest. Management of Patmohona Colliery, Sodepur Area, ECL is directed 
to fix the pay of Prakash Chandra Panda by granting one additional increment @ three percent in basic w.e.f. 
01/11/2011 by treating his posting to the post of Looseman, Cat-IV as promotion instead of regularization. Arrears of 
the incremental benefit be paid within three months from the date of communication of order. Let an Award be drawn 
up in the light of my above discussion. Let copies of Award be communicated to the Ministry for information and 
Notification.

2 The averments made in the petition in brief are as follows:

procedure, he submitted applications dated 22.1.1996, 25.9.1997 and 5.12.1998 to the second and third Respondents
